correctness.rationale: All faces are exhausted by five mutually coherent families for arbitrary \(a,b\ge3\) and \(t\ge1\). Each one of \((a-1)t\) mixed edges has its unique triangle coface; after exact elementary collapses the remaining two simplex shores and cone form a contractible core, with exactly \((a-1)(b-t)\) independent one-cell attachments. Zero faults reduce to two contractible shores linked by ab edges. Explicit integral cycles generate H1, survive through preceding stages, and give split surjections with primitive kernels. Finite exhaustive enumeration across 72 triples independently corroborated the face and boundary claims; it is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural and nontrivial question is fault-incidence dependence of the topology of second-independence complexes: the exact all-size integral filtered homotopy answer, split no-birth maps, and full surviving permutation lattice quantify a sharp clustered-vs-disjoint change. For three faults \(K_{5,5}\) star deletion yields eight circles, whereas matching deletion yields four circles and a two-sphere; hence a qualitative topology transition is sensitive to fault clustering, not merely deletion count.
